dish: the Ikebana / Grand Yozora tasting menu (ikejime fish, seasonal Grand Est produce)
address: 1 Parvis des Droits de l'Homme, 57000 Metz, France
w: Perched atop the Centre Pompidou-Metz, chef Charles Coulombeau's Yozora won a MICHELIN star in 2025, just nine months after opening — the only starred restaurant inside a museum in France. A precise French cuisine sourced on well-raised local produce and shaded with the chef's years in Japan, served as two tasting menus (12-course Ikebana, 16-course Grand Yozora).

dish: the blind seasonal tasting menus of creative Lorraine cuisine
w: An institutional table on the Place de Chambre below the cathedral, where Maître Restaurateur Alexis Baudin cooks a local, seasonal and creative gastronomy through four blind menus (including a vegetarian one). A Gault&Millau toque and one of Metz's most reliable bench-mark kitchens.

dish: house-made fresh pasta (tortelli, ravioli) and burrata
w: A refined Italian table in the Outre-Seille quarter, ten minutes from the Centre Pompidou, listed by Gault&Millau and the MICHELIN Guide and holding the Maître Restaurateur title. Carefully sourced Italian and Provençal product — charcuterie, burrata, wild fish, pure-bred meats — around house pasta.

dish: natural-wine flights with charcuterie and cheese boards
w: A convivial bar à vin on the Place de Chambre with a cathedral-view terrace, pouring more than 500 wines — 80% organic and natural — alongside a small kitchen of charcuterie and cheese to share. A Gault&Millau-listed favourite of the Metz wine crowd.

dish: market bistronomie plates on the Place de la Comédie terrace
address: 4 Place de la Comédie, 57000 Metz, France
w: Set in the former Saint-Marcel military pavilion of 1752 facing the opera-theatre, El Theatris serves inventive market bistronomie with wines by the glass and a large terrace on the pale cobbles of the Place de la Comédie. A Gault&Millau-listed city fixture.

dish: fresh Tuscan tortelli and truffle carbonara
w: A tiny vaulted-cellar trattoria in the Outre-Seille tanners' district where chef Luca cooks Tuscan food — fresh tortelli and ravioli, a signature truffle carbonara, grilled octopus, Italian charcuterie — with Chianti. A genuine hidden gem, cross-checked at a very high rating volume.
A traditional Lebanese table in a quiet lane at the foot of the cathedral, serving delicate mezze — creamy houmous, crisp falafel, fresh taboulé — that anchor Metz's lively Levantine dining scene.

address: 19 Rue Dupont des Loges, 57000 Metz, France
w: A minimalist family osteria opened in 2021 by a Sicilian couple, Caterina and Armando Fasano, near the cathedral; everything from antipasti to desserts is made on site, and locals rate it among the city's most authentic Italian rooms.

address: 2 Rue du Moyen Pont, 57000 Metz, France
w: A modern crêperie on the pedestrian Rue du Moyen Pont near the cathedral, turning out buckwheat galettes bretonnes and revisited sweet crêpes with fresh local product in an Anglo-rock room. A reliable, well-rated stop for a casual Breton lunch in the centre.

address: 17 Rue du Grand Cerf, 57000 Metz, France
w: On the pedestrian Rue du Grand Cerf, the Metz house of Pascal Caffet — Meilleur Ouvrier de France Pâtissier-Chocolatier and World Champion of Dessert Arts — in the premises of the historic Fresson pâtisserie. Fine chocolates, macarons and entremets to the highest craft standard.

dish: the mirabelle macaron and pâte d'amande à la mirabelle
w: A Metz maître chocolatier carrying the MOSL quality label, known for macarons in delicate original flavours — above all the mirabelle macaron built on Lorraine's emblematic plum — plus mirabelle almond paste and regional sweets made in the workshop behind the shop.

dish: choucroute and seafood platters (plateau de fruits de mer)
w: Opened in 1911 and classified a Monument Historique since 1976, the 'Excel' is a jewel of Art Nouveau — interiors by Gruber, Majorelle and Daum, a living tribute to the École de Nancy — and a great French brasserie of choucroute and seafood platters near Nancy station.

dish: modern Lorraine tasting menu (ikejime Vosges char, Bresse chicken)
w: A MICHELIN-starred mansion abutting the opera just behind Place Stanislas, where chef Charles Coulombeau and his wife Roxane run a modern cuisine touched by Japan — citrus and Asian notes paired with premium product like ikejime Vosges Arctic char or Bresse chicken. One Michelin star, three Gault&Millau toques.

dish: the macarons de Nancy (1793 recipe) and bergamote de Nancy
w: In the pedestrian streets by Place Stanislas, the house that has perpetuated since 1793 the macaron de Nancy — a secret recipe of egg white, sugar and Provence almonds inherited from two Benedictine sisters. Labelled Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant; also the IGP Bergamote de Nancy.

dish: bergamotes de Nancy IGP and macarons de Nancy
w: Founded in 1840, the oldest confectioner in Lorraine and Alsace — 'Au Duché de Lorraine' — keeper of the bergamote de Nancy, the hard bergamot-scented sweet, alongside macarons de Nancy and regional specialities, in a beautifully preserved 19th-century shop near the station.
